4//! Layer management for filter effects rendering.
5//!
6//! This module provides infrastructure for managing persistent layer buffers
7//! that can be rendered to independently and then composited together. This is
8//! necessary for spatial filter effects that require access to a fully-rendered
9//! layer (e.g., Gaussian blur).
10//!
11//! Layers are stored as Pixmap instances (row-major, u8 RGBA format), which
12//! allows efficient filter operations without layout conversion overhead.
13//! Each layer maintains its own bounding box in wide tile coordinates, allowing
14//! efficient memory usage for layers that don't span the entire render target.
15
16use crate::third_party::vello_common::coarse::WideTilesBbox;
17use crate::third_party::vello_common::pixmap::Pixmap;
18use crate::third_party::vello_cpu::region::Region;
19use hashbrown::HashMap;
20
21/// Manages persistent layer storage for filter effects.
22///
23/// Each layer is allocated as a `Pixmap` with row-major RGBA8 format.
24/// This eliminates conversion overhead for filter operations.
25#[derive(Debug)]
26pub struct LayerManager {
27    /// Map of layer ID to (Pixmap, wtile bounding box).
28    /// The Pixmap contains the layer's pixel data, and the Bbox defines which
29    /// wide tiles this layer occupies (in wide tile coordinates).
30    layers: HashMap<u32, (Pixmap, WideTilesBbox)>,
31    /// Next available layer ID for automatic allocation.
32    next_id: u32,
33    /// Reusable scratch buffer for filter operations that need temporary storage.
34    /// Examples include separable convolution passes (e.g., Gaussian blur) or
35    /// intermediate compositing results. This buffer is lazily allocated and
36    /// automatically resized as needed to avoid repeated allocations.
37    scratch_buffer: Option<Pixmap>,
38}
39
40impl Default for LayerManager {
41    /// Creates a new, empty layer manager with no allocated layers.
42    ///
43    /// Layer IDs start from 1 (ID 0 is reserved for internal use).
44    fn default() -> Self {
45        Self { layers: HashMap::new(), next_id: 1, scratch_buffer: None }
46    }
47}
48
49impl LayerManager {
50    /// Create a new, empty layer manager.
51    ///
52    /// Layers can be registered on-demand using [`register_layer`](Self::register_layer).
53    pub fn new() -> Self {
54        Self::default()
55    }
56
57    /// Register a layer with a specific ID, wide tile bounding box, and pixel data.
58    ///
59    /// The provided `Pixmap` should already contain the layer's pixel data (e.g., the
60    /// result of rendering a layer or applying a filter effect).
61    ///
62    /// If a layer with this ID already exists, this method does nothing (no replacement).
63    ///
64    /// # Parameters
65    /// - `layer_id`: A unique identifier for this layer. Layer ID 0 is reserved for internal use.
66    /// - `wtile_bbox`: The bounding box of the layer in wide tile coordinates. This defines
67    ///   the region of the layer that contains valid pixel data, enabling efficient memory
68    ///   usage for layers that don't span the entire render target.
69    /// - `pixmap`: The pixel data for this layer in row-major RGBA8 format.
70    pub fn register_layer(&mut self, layer_id: u32, wtile_bbox: WideTilesBbox, pixmap: Pixmap) {
71        self.layers.insert(layer_id, (pixmap, wtile_bbox));
72
73        if layer_id >= self.next_id {
74            self.next_id = layer_id + 1;
75        }
76    }
77
78    /// Get a mutable `Region` view into a specific wide tile within a layer.
79    ///
80    /// This extracts a tile-sized region from the layer's Pixmap, allowing
81    /// rendering or compositing operations on individual tiles without copying
82    /// pixel data. The returned Region provides a mutable view into the underlying
83    /// layer buffer.
84    ///
85    /// Returns [`None`] if:
86    /// - The layer doesn't exist
87    /// - The tile position is outside the layer's bounding box
88    /// - The tile extraction fails (e.g., invalid coordinates)
89    ///
90    /// # Parameters
91    /// - `layer_id`: The ID of the layer to access
92    /// - `tile_x`: The x-coordinate of the wide tile in global wide tile coordinates
93    /// - `tile_y`: The y-coordinate of the wide tile in global wide tile coordinates
94    ///
95    /// # Coordinate Systems
96    /// The input coordinates (`tile_x`, `tile_y`) are in *global* wide tile space,
97    /// but they are automatically converted to *local* coordinates relative to the
98    /// layer's bounding box before extracting the region.
99    pub fn layer_tile_region_mut(&mut self, layer_id: u32, tile_x: u16, tile_y: u16) -> Option<Region<'_>> {
100        let (pixmap, bbox) = self.layers.get_mut(&layer_id)?;
101
102        // Ensure the requested tile is within the layer's allocated bounds
103        if !bbox.contains(tile_x, tile_y) {
104            return None;
105        }
106
107        // Convert global tile coordinates to layer-local (bbox-relative) coordinates
108        let local_x = tile_x - bbox.x0();
109        let local_y = tile_y - bbox.y0();
110
111        // Extract a mutable Region view of the tile from the underlying pixmap
112        Region::from_pixmap_tile(pixmap, local_x, local_y)
113    }
114
115    /// Get or create a scratch buffer of at least the requested dimensions.
116    ///
117    /// This buffer is reused across filter operations to minimize allocations.
118    /// If the existing buffer is large enough, it's reused; otherwise, a new
119    /// (larger) buffer is allocated.
120    ///
121    /// # Parameters
122    /// - `width`: Minimum width in pixels
123    /// - `height`: Minimum height in pixels
124    ///
125    /// # Returns
126    /// A mutable reference to a `Pixmap` of at least `width × height` pixels.
127    /// The actual buffer may be larger than requested if it was previously allocated
128    /// with larger dimensions.
129    pub fn get_scratch_buffer(&mut self, width: u16, height: u16) -> &mut Pixmap {
130        match &mut self.scratch_buffer {
131            None => {
132                // No buffer exists yet, allocate a new one
133                self.scratch_buffer = Some(Pixmap::new(width, height));
134            }
135            Some(buf) if buf.width() < width || buf.height() < height => {
136                // Existing buffer is too small, resize it
137                buf.resize(width, height);
138            }
139            // Buffer is already large enough, reuse it without reallocation
140            Some(_) => {}
141        }
142
143        self.scratch_buffer.as_mut().unwrap()
144    }
145}
